results.title: 'Sumbakkokjil' producer serves Korean ghost lore to K-pop's global fandom
results.content: By pairing K-pop idols with Korean horror, "Sumbakkokjil" has grown from the first original program on Mnet Plus, CJ ENM's global K-pop platform, into its flagship, drawing fans around the world who tune in for their favorite acts and stay for the scares. "Sumbakkokjil" — the Korean name for the game of hide-and-seek — drops K-pop acts into abandoned buildings and other darkened sets. Group members must avoid being caught by an unidentified seeker for 4,444 seconds. In its first season, they hunted for keys before the chase began, while season two required them to collect "dead pieces" to escape. Rather than the typical showcase of singing and dancing, the show focuses on how idols react to the scares and how they look out for one another. results.title: Korean, Mongolian FMs discuss cooperation on critical minerals, trade
results.content: The top diplomats of Korea and Mongolia discussed bilateral cooperation on critical minerals, trade, technology and other key issues during their talks in Seoul on Monday, the foreign ministry said. Foreign Minister Cho Hyun met with Mongolian Foreign Minister Batmunkh Battsetseg at his ministry as the two countries seek to expand cooperation following Korean President Lee Jae Myung's state visit to Ulaanbaatar in July. During the meeting, Cho called for accelerating joint efforts to sign a comprehensive economic partnership agreement (CEPA), noting that the agreement, if inked, would serve as an institutional foundation for expanding bilateral trade and investment, according to the ministry. results.title: 2-term lawmaker nominated to lead interior ministry
results.content: Rep. Han Jun-ho, tapped to lead the interior ministry, is a two-term lawmaker of the ruling Democratic Party of Korea (DPK) who formerly worked as a news anchor. Born in 1974 in the southwestern city of Jeonju, Han graduated from Yonsei University with a degree in mathematics before joining local broadcaster MBC as a newscaster in 2003. He left MBC in 2018 and worked at the presidential office under then President Moon Jae-in as a communications official. Han was elected as a lawmaker for the DPK in the 2020 general elections before winning his second term in the 2024 elections. He currently serves as a ranking member of the parliamentary science, ICT, broadcasting and communications committee. results.title: Kim Myung-min returns as ruthless jungle boss in 'Tristes Tropiques'
results.content: For veteran actor Kim Myung-min, returning to the big screen after a seven-year absence did not feel like a long wait at all. "To be honest, I didn't realize it had been seven years until I saw it in news reports," Kim told The Korea Times at a cafe in Seoul, Monday. "Back when I was younger, even two or three years felt like forever. Now that I am in my 50s, time flies at the speed of light." Kim stars as Master in director Park Hoon-jung's upcoming action noir "Tristes Tropiques," whose French title translates to "sad tropics." The movie marks Kim's first movie appearance since 2019 and his first project since the 2024 ENA drama "Your Honor." It also reunites him with Park nine years after they worked together on the 2017 crime thriller "V.I.P." results.title: 3-term lawmaker with N. Korea expertise tapped as unification minister
results.content: Unification Minister nominee Hong Ihk-pyo is a three-term lawmaker and a close political ally of President Lee Jae Myung with North Korea expertise. Born in 1967, he studied political science at Hanyang University. Before entering politics, he worked as a researcher at the Korea Institute for International Economic Policy and as a policy adviser to the Ministry of Unification. He also taught as a professor at the University of North Korean Studies. He won election to the National Assembly three times, serving from 2012 to 2024. Hong served as floor leader of the ruling Democratic Party of Korea from September 2023 to May 2024 when Lee was party chair. Earlier this year, Hong was appointed as senior presidential secretary for political affairs, handling coordination with the National Assembly and the political parties. At that time, the president described Hong as "reasonable and amicable

results.title: Critic-turned-presidential spokesperson nominated as culture minister
results.content: Kang Yu-jung, the senior presidential spokesperson nominated as culture minister Monday, is a cultural specialist who worked for nearly two decades as a film and literary critic and columnist. Kang, 51, first gained prominence in 2005 when she swept three prizes in that year's newspaper literary contests, winning in film criticism from the Dong-A Ilbo and in literary criticism from the Chosun Ilbo and the Kyunghyang Shinmun. As a critic and columnist, Kang regularly appeared on television programs about film and wrote for daily newspapers. She also published several books on cinema and taught at Korea University and Kangnam University. Her interest in the arts extended beyond criticism. Last year, she received a special award at the Korea Dance Awards in recognition of her support for dance and her contributions to developing and popularizing the art form. results.title: Ex-diplomat well versed in US, N. Korea tapped as foreign minister
results.content: Foreign Minister nominee Lim Woong-soon, currently a senior presidential security official, is a former veteran diplomat well versed in relations with the United States and diplomacy with North Korea. Since President Lee Jae Myung took office in June last year, Lim has served as the second deputy director of the National Security Office at Cheong Wa Dae, assisting the president in making key foreign policy and security decisions. His nomination came as South Korea's chief diplomat faces a host of foreign policy tasks, ranging from implementing security, trade and investment agreements with the U.S. to handling North Korea-related diplomacy and ensuring cooperation with China, Japan and other countries. results.title: Korea's exports forecast to exceed $1 tril. for 2nd straight year in 2027
results.content: Korea's exports are expected to exceed $1 trillion for the second consecutive year in 2027 on continued global demand for semiconductors, a state-run think tank said Monday. The Korea Institute for Industrial Economics & Trade (KIET) forecast that Korea will post $1.32 trillion in exports in 2027, up 14.1 percent from this year's estimate of $1.16 trillion. The trade surplus is expected to rise to $455.9 billion next year from $377.8 billion this year. The KIET said exports are expected to expand 33.9 percent on-year in the first half of 2027, driven by increasing investment in artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure, while they are forecast to contract 0.7 percent in the second half due to a base effect and a correction in memory chip prices. results.title: Unification minister, Mongolian FM vow closer cooperation for peace on Korean Peninsula
results.content: Unification Minister Chung Dong-young on Monday asked Mongolia to support peace on the Korean Peninsula, citing its friendly ties with the two Koreas, during a meeting with Mongolian Foreign Minister Batmunkh Battsetseg, the ministry said. Chung noted Mongolia's efforts to promote regional peace and thanked Battsetseg for the warm welcome he received in June when he visited the country to attend the 11th Ulaanbaatar Dialogue on Northeast Asian Security. Describing bilateral relations as entering an "age of gold," he expressed hope that the two countries will keep deepening mutual ties. Battsetseg also vowed to continue close cooperation with Seoul in its push for peaceful coexistence on the peninsula, according to the ministry.

results.title: Seoul stocks lose 3.3% as AI rout tests gov't rescue plans
results.content: Korean stocks fell 3.31 percent Monday, as a sell-off in artificial intelligence (AI)-related shares deepened, though bargain hunting after steep losses and government preparations to activate a stock market stabilization fund helped limit the decline. The benchmark KOSPI closed at 4,708.54, down 3.31 percent, its lowest finish since Jan. 13. The index opened 2.77 percent lower and plunged as much as 5 percent intraday, briefly slipping to 4,586.8. A sell-side sidecar was triggered at 11:33 a.m. The index pared losses in afternoon trading to finish just above the 4,700 mark. Institutional and other corporate investors helped cushion the decline as foreign and retail investors continued to sell, according to analysts. results.title: FC Seoul treats 100 families with 3 or more kids to K League title celebration
results.content: FC Seoul is turning its long-awaited championship celebration into a family affair, offering 100 Seoul households free tickets to its upcoming home match as the city expands efforts to make professional sports more accessible. The Seoul Metropolitan Government said Monday it will invite about 400 people from large families to FC Seoul's match against Daejeon Hana Citizen at Seoul World Cup Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 28, at 2 p.m. The invitation comes after FC Seoul secured its first K League 1 championship in 10 years, with the city and club joining forces to celebrate the milestone with local residents. Eligible applicants must live in Seoul and have at least two children, with the youngest aged 18 or younger. results.content: The ongoing restrictions on intelligence sharing between South Korea and the United States could spiral into a full-blown security crisis if not resolved quickly and Seoul must strengthen ties with Washington and Tokyo to counter the deepening North Korea-China-Russia axis, the chairman of the National Assembly’s Foreign Affairs and Unification Committee said. “Korea is currently experiencing dissonance with the U.S. in intelligence cooperation, which could escalate into a grave security crisis if not restored quickly,” Rep. results.title: Former longtime SC Bank Korea chief tapped to head banking lobby
results.content: Park Jong-bok, former CEO of Standard Chartered (SC) Bank Korea, has been named the sole candidate to lead the Korea Federation of Banks, setting him up to become the next head of the banking lobby, the federation said Monday. The federation's chairman recommendation committee selected Park from its pool of candidates at its third meeting. It is scheduled to hold a general meeting Thursday to formally elect its next chairman. The committee said Park was well qualified to address the challenges facing the banking industry and help it navigate growing uncertainties, citing his broad understanding of the financial sector. Born in 1955 in Cheongju, North Chungcheong Province, Park graduated from Cheongju High School and Kyung Hee University's economics department. results.title: Stray Kids' Felix brings fresh energy to Korean hanbok
results.content: Felix of K-pop group Stray Kids is putting a modern face on traditional Korean clothing, called "hanbok," joining five local designers in a fashion campaign set to reach audiences in six major cities around the world. The Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism said Monday it had unveiled the 2026 Hanbok Wave campaign, featuring the internationally popular singer in a series of photographs showcasing contemporary interpretations of traditional Korean dress. The project, organized with the Korea Craft and Design Foundation, pairs promising domestic hanbok brands with prominent figures from Korean popular culture to reinterpret traditional clothing for modern audiences and promote it internationally. results.title: S. Korea commemorates 16th anniv. of victory against N. Korea's 2010 shelling of border island
results.content: The Marine Corps on Monday held a ceremony to mark the 16th anniversary of South Korea's victory in an artillery attack in 2010 by North Korea on a border island that killed two soldiers and two civilians. The ceremony was held at Daejeon National Cemetery in Daejeon, some 140 kilometers south of Seoul, on the occasion of the 16th anniversary of the North's artillery attack on Yeonpyeong Island on Nov. 23, 2010. North Korea's shelling of the island marked its first attack on a civilian area in the South since the 1950-53 Korean War. During Monday's event, Vice Defense Minister Lee Doo-hee said the South Korean military will maintain a robust readiness posture to ensure its victory against any enemy threats. results.title: Court holds arrest warrant hearings for 8 election officials
results.content: A court on Monday held arrest warrant hearings for eight National Election Commission (NEC) officials accused of manipulating voter turnout numbers or tampering with vote count records during the June 3 local elections. Three officials from the NEC headquarters appeared at the Seoul Central District Court in the morning, refusing to answer reporters' questions before entering the courtroom. Hearings for the remaining five officials from regional NEC offices were set to be held later in the afternoon. The court was expected to decide whether to issue the warrants later in the day at the earliest. results.title: Factional feud, impeachment fight test Kim Min-seok's DPK leadership at 100 days
results.content: Ruling Democratic Party of Korea (DPK) Chairman Kim Min-seok heads into his 100th day in office on Tuesday, as party support slips amid a deepening factional feud, in stark contrast to the turnaround he promised. Kim pledged during his leadership campaign to raise the DPK’s support by at least 10 percentage points within three months. But a Gallup Korea poll released on Friday put the DPK’s support at 36 percent, down from 41 percent in a survey conducted from Aug. 11–13, just before Kim took office on Aug. 17. Under the circumstances, Kim’s leadership will face another test as he tries to reunite the DPK and win over centrist voters while the party’s hard-liners push to impeach Supreme Court Chief Justice Cho Hee-dae — a move that could rally its base and alienate moderates. “It appears the voters still don’t feel they can count on the ruling party to settle problems under Kim’s leaders

results.title: GS E&C joins hands with 3 firms to speed up data center construction
results.content: GS E&C has signed a memorandum of understanding (MOU) with LS Electric, LG Uplus and Honeywell to shorten the time needed to bring data centers into service by coordinating engineering work from procurement through final testing. GS E&C announced Monday that the four companies had signed the MOU in Seoul. The construction company said rising demand for data centers amid the expansion of the artificial intelligence (AI) industry has made meeting customers' project schedules more important than ever. The partners will coordinate across four stages: procurement preparation, design, system installation and integrated commissioning. They will review power, design, construction, controls and operational requirements early in the process to avoid duplicated work and address operational needs before construction begins. results.title: Family of late LEET top scorer appears before police in cheating probe
results.content: A family member of the late top scorer of this year's law school entrance exam appeared before police Monday as investigators step up a probe into allegations that he cheated on the test. The late Lee Jin-woo, a 32-year-old dental student, was found dead Thursday after facing suspicions of cheating by using artificial intelligence (AI) to earn a perfect score on the Legal Education Eligibility Test (LEET). Despite his death, police have pressed ahead with the investigation on suspicion of fraud and other charges, after a group of lawyers earlier filed a police complaint. Earlier in the day, a family member of Lee appeared before the financial crime unit under the Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency. results.title: Hotel Shilla CEO Lee Boo-jin's son takes mother's surname after turning 19
results.content: The son of Hotel Shilla CEO Lee Boo-jin, a member of Samsung's founding family, has legally changed his surname to his mother's after reaching adulthood, following a court-approved application he filed himself. According to legal sources Monday, the Seoul Family Court approved a petition filed by Lee's son, Dong-hyun, to change his surname from Lim, his father's family name, to Lee. Presiding Judge Park Mi-hwa of the court's Family Division 21 granted the request last month. Dong-hyun reportedly filed the petition after becoming a legal adult in August. During its review, the court also sought the opinion of his father, Lim Woo-jae, a former adviser to Samsung Electro-Mechanics. Under Article 781, Paragraph 6 of Korea's Civil Act, a child's surname and ancestral family origin may be changed with court approval if deemed necessary for the child's welfare. results.title: 'Cats' unveils international cast for 8-city Korea tour
results.content: The international touring production of “Cats” will visit eight Korean cities beginning in December, bringing a 29-member cast whose performances combine singing with the demanding physical work of transforming into felines. The tour opens at Daegu’s Keimyung Art Center on Dec. 18 and continues through April 11, 2027, concluding at the Sejong Center for the Performing Arts in Seoul, according to a press release announcing the cast and itinerary, Monday. The principal performers have traveled with the production since its South African opening in December 2025, followed by the musical’s Mumbai premiere and engagements in Hong Kong and Singapore. Cindy-Ann Abrahams will play Grizabella, the faded glamour cat. results.title: Korea's gender wage gap remains widest among OECD members
results.content: Korea continued to have the widest gender pay gap among OECD countries in 2025, with women's median earnings 27.8 percent lower than men's, data showed Monday. According to the latest OECD data, women's median earnings in Korea stood at 72.2 percent of men's last year. The gap was the largest among 13 OECD countries that have released figures for 2025, exceeding Japan's 20.1 percent and the United States' 17.9 percent. The figures for Korea cover full-time employees and compare median monthly earnings. They do not adjust for differences in occupations or job assignments. Korea has recorded the widest gender pay gap among OECD members every year since 2000, although the disparity has gradually narrowed. results.content: President Lee Jae Myung nominated former Justice Minister Kang Kum-sil to head the National Intelligence Service (NIS), Monday. Lee also tapped Lim Woong-soon, his second deputy national security adviser and a former ambassador to Canada, as foreign minister, and Hong Ihk-pyo, a former presidential secretary for political affairs and former floor leader of the ruling Democratic Party of Korea (DPK), as unification minister. Presidential chief of staff Lim Kwang-hyun announced the Cabinet reshuffle largely focused on the security and diplomacy sectors during a briefing at Cheong Wa Dae in Seoul. results.title: Korea ready to deploy market stabilization fund if conditions warrant: finance minister
results.content: Korea will decide whether to deploy its stock market stabilization fund based on how market conditions evolve, Minister of Finance and Economy Lee Hyoung-il said Monday, a day after the government began preparations. Lee said the government would continue to monitor the market before deciding on the timing and size of any deployment. “We are reviewing the steps needed in case market conditions warrant activating the fund,” Lee said at a press conference. “We will decide on the details as we assess how the situation evolves.” Lee said the review was intended to ensure the fund could be deployed smoothly if needed, given how long it had been idle. Asked whether the government would expand the fund, he said authorities would assess market conditions at the time of any deployment before deciding on its size. results.title: NC raises 2026 sales forecast on Lineage Classic success
results.content: Korean game developer NC raised its sales forecast for this year to 2.8 trillion won ($2.09 billion) in a Nov. 11 regulatory filing after sales through September surpassed the lower end of its previous full-year guidance, as Lineage Classic and casual mobile games bolstered its results. Third-quarter sales rose 91 percent from a year earlier to 687 billion won, while the company returned to operating profitability, posting an operating profit of 120 billion won. Sales for the first nine months rose 83 percent to 2.01 trillion won, above the previous guidance floor of 2 trillion won. Lineage Classic generated 159 billion won in sales in the third quarter, bringing its cumulative sales to 428 billion won in about eight months after launch. results.title: Senior Qatari official calls Korea 'essential' partner in post-oil era
results.content: A senior Qatari official has described Korea as an "essential" partner in Qatar's efforts to diversify its industries in the post-oil era during a bilateral policy meeting in Doha, Seoul's foreign ministry said Monday. Qatar's Minister of State for Foreign Affairs Sultan bin Saad Al Muraikhi made the remarks during the meeting with Seoul's Deputy Minister for Political Affairs Chung Eui-hae on Sunday (local time), highlighting Doha's priority on maintaining cooperation with the Asian country. Chung asked Doha to help ensure that Korean companies can operate without difficulties in Qatar, noting that they have honored their commitments, including meeting project schedules, despite wartime conditions in the Middle East, according to the ministry. results.title: Daily share buyback limit to be lifted for 3 months amid market rout
results.content: The country's financial regulator said Monday it will lift the daily share buyback limit for listed firms for three months, as part of efforts to stem market volatility. According to the Financial Services Commission (FSC), the daily limit for the purchase of own shares by publicly traded companies will be fully lifted from Tuesday. On Sunday, the financial authorities announced a set of measures to limit market jitters caused by rising fears over artificial intelligence (AI)-related investments. They also said around 10 trillion won ($7.42 billion) worth of a stock stabilization fund is in store to be activated when necessary. If the market rout deepens, the fund will go into operation, marking the first time since 2008. results.title: Jongno District deploys AI crosswalks to give slower pedestrians more time
results.content: Jongno District in central Seoul is upgrading its intersections with artificial intelligence (AI), pavement-level LED lights and automated voice alerts to help pedestrians — especially children and older adults — cross streets more safely. The district office said it will begin operating pavement-mounted pedestrian signals and voice guidance devices at 123 locations from Dec. 1 with an AI-powered system that automatically extends crossing time. The pavement-level pedestrian signals illuminate the tactile pavers, a kind of ground surface indicator to assist disabled pedestrians, at crosswalks to help people detect when it is safe to cross. Voice guidance devices use infrared sensors to detect pedestrians and issue audible warnings when they attempt to cross against the signal, as well as announcing when the light turns green. results.title: US Forces Korea deploys Apache, Blackhawk helicopters for live-fire drills in Japan
results.content: The U.S. Forces Korea (USFK) recently deployed its helicopters for live-fire drills in Japan, the first time such assets have been sent outside the Korean Peninsula for exercises, the USFK said Monday. The 2nd Infantry Division's 2nd Combat Aviation Brigade deployed the AH-64E Apache attack helicopters, the UH-60 Black Hawk multirole utility helicopters and the CH-47 Chinook transport helicopters to the Combined Arms Training Center (CATC) at Camp Fuji, located in Shizuoka Prefecture, the USFK said in a social media post. It said the "historic first" deployment of the choppers was aimed at strengthening its readiness in the Indo-Pacific. results.title: PPP files petition with Constitutional Court over special counsel bill
results.content: Lawmakers of the main opposition People Power Party (PPP) filed a petition with the Constitutional Court on Monday, arguing that their rights to vote on legislation were violated by the ruling Democratic Party of Korea (DPK)'s unilateral passage of a special counsel bill. The PPP's move came after the DPK-controlled National Assembly railroaded the bill earlier this month that mandates a special counsel investigation into suspicions that prosecutors under the previous administration had indicted President Lee Jae Myung and others on fabricated evidence. PPP lawmakers had boycotted the vote in protest. The PPP claimed that its lawmakers were not given sufficient time to review and deliberate on the details of the bill before its passage and said it filed a competence dispute against National Assembly Speaker Cho Jeong-sik and DPK Rep.
